record.paper_title: Selected open problems in Matching Under Preferences
record.context_brief: solvability probability for random stable roommates
record.original_question: For a uniformly random Stable Roommates instance of size n, determine the probability p_n that the instance admits a stable matching, especially its asymptotic behavior as n grows large.

evidence.quote: A long-standing open problem, formulated as Problem 8 in Gusfield and Irving [45], is the computation of pn, the probability that a random instance, chosen uniformly from all possible sr instances of size n, admits a stable matching. Of particular interest is the asymptotic behaviour of pn, as n grows large.

artifact.self_contained_problem: Consider the Stable Roommates problem of size n (with n even): there are n agents, and each agent has a strict preference ranking (a total order) over the other n−1 agents. A matching is a partition of the agents into n/2 disjoint unordered pairs. A pair of agents {a,b} that are not matched to each other forms a blocking pair if a strictly prefers b to its current partner and b strictly prefers a to its current partner. A matching is stable if it admits no blocking pair. An instance of size n is chosen uniformly at random from all ((n−1)!)^n possible profiles of preference lists (equivalently, each agent's preference list is an independent uniformly random permutation of the other n−1 agents). Let p_n denote the probability that such a uniformly random instance admits at least one stable matching. Determine p_n, and in particular determine the asymptotic behavior of p_n as n → ∞.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of computing p_n exactly is classically open (Problem 8 of Gusfield–Irving). Pittel–Irving (1994) gave a non-trivial constant upper bound e^{1/2}/2 ≈ 0.8244 and a lower bound of order n^{-1/2}. A recent preprint ("The random stable roommates problem typically has no solution", arXiv:2601.07612) proves that p_n → 0 as n → ∞, confirming the Gusfield–Irving conjecture; however, the exact asymptotic rate (simulations suggest Θ(n^{-1/4})) and a closed-form for p_n remain undetermined.

status_evidence.title: The random stable roommates problem typically has no solution
status_evidence.snippet: first vanishing upper bound on the probability that a stable matching exists, confirming the conjecture of Gusfield and Irving
status_evidence.claim: It has been proven that p_n → 0, but the precise asymptotic remains open.

status_evidence.title: The 'Stable Roommates' Problem with Random Preferences (Pittel & Irving)
status_evidence.snippet: the probability a stable matching exists is greater than or equal to (4e^3/πn)^{1/2}
status_evidence.claim: Earlier bounds gave constant upper bound and Ω(n^{-1/2}) lower bound on p_n.

status_evidence.title: Stable Roommates Problem with Random Preferences (Mertens)
status_evidence.snippet: simulation data suggest that the true rate of convergence is Θ(n^{-1/4})
status_evidence.claim: Numerical evidence suggests p_n decays like n^{-1/4} but this is unproven.
